title: SCIM transactional provisioning with finalizer-based deprovision orchestration
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Problem: We continue to see edge-case failures during SCIM-driven user and group deprovisioning that lead to orphaned resources in downstream systems (datastores, analytics, third-party connectors). Incidents usually happen when retries, partial failures, or concurrent SCIM delta syncs race with deprovision requests. Current heuristics-based retries (cron/backfill) are noisy and produce duplicate work with incomplete audit trails.

Goal: Implement a transactional, observable provisioning pipeline that uses an operation log and 'finalizer' orchestration to ensure: idempotent operations, clear handoff to downstream consumers, reliable deprovision (including graceful quarantine window), and a complete audit trail that ties SCIM operations to downstream acknowledgements. The design must reduce orphan rate, improve SLO for deprovision completion, and provide operators with deterministic remediation tools.
acceptance_criteria: SCIM create/update/delete operations are appended to a provision_log table with an idempotency key derived from the SCIM externalId and the request-id header.
A finalizer field is added to user/group resources (scim.finalizers) and prevents delete until downstream acknowledgements are received or a configurable TTL elapses.
Deprovision flow supports lease-based worker claiming so multiple workers cannot double-process the same job within a lease window.

Retries use exponential backoff with full jitter and are driven by the operation log state rather than uncontrolled requeues; retry attempts and outcomes are emitted to audit logs and console metrics.
End-to-end tests simulate transient downstream failures and show no orphaned entries after retry/backfill window and that audit events were emitted for every transition.
Migration plan in place to backfill finalizers for existing users and a one-time reconcile job to populate the operation log for active deletion tokens.
Performance: additional SCIM write latency < 45ms median and < 150ms p95 for the provision_log append on peak provisioning traffic (validated under load test).
technical_design:
Overview: Introduce a small provisioning orchestration service (provision-orch) that sits between the SCIM API layer and downstream consumers. On SCIM write, the API will perform two actions in a transactional pattern: 1) append an operation record to provision_log (operation-id, externalId, op-type, payload, idempotency_key, created_at, state=queued) and 2) if op-type==delete, add 'scim:finalizer:pending_deprovision' to the user resource. The append is the canonical source of truth for in-flight operations.

Operation Log & Idempotency: The provision_log record uses a composite unique constraint on (idempotency_key, op-type) to ensure duplicate SCIM retries do not create multiple operations. Each operation transitions through states: queued -> claimed -> in_progress -> success | failed | quarantined. Workers claim operations by performing an atomic compare-and-set using the operation id + lease token (optimistic concurrency). Leases expire after configurable TTL for retries. Workers record attempt metadata and error classes to the record and emit structured audit events for each attempt.

Finalizers and Quarantine: For deletes, the finalizer prevents immediate resource tombstoning. The worker will execute downstream deprovision steps (datastore remove, third-party API calls, analytics dim updates) and only when all required ack events are observed will it remove the finalizer and mark operation success. If a downstream system cannot ack within 'quarantine_window' the operation moves to quarantined state and an alert is raised for manual remediation. A configurable 'force-delete-after' TTL allows automatic finalizer removal if operator policy permits (audit logged).

Audit Logging: Every state transition and downstream acknowledgement is emitted synchronously to the central audit service with the operation-id and a signed event id. Audit records include operator, request-id, source-system, attempt_count, error-class, and downstream-ack ids. The audit pipeline is appended as part of the operation transaction where possible; when the audit service is unavailable, we fall back to durable local queue and increment the operation record's pending_audit_count.

Backoff & Retry Strategy: Use exponential backoff with full jitter for retries, capped attempts configurable per downstream integration. Implement classification of transient vs permanent errors (4xx permanent vs 5xx transient + network). Retries are orchestrated from the operation_log state machine so we can inspect history and avoid blind replays.

Migration: Backfill job reads active users with no finalizer and creates a 'noop' delete-check operation for users with deprovision markers, and optionally adds finalizer flags for all users in scope. A reconciliation pass will create operation_log entries for recent deletion events (last 90 days) to seed historical evidence for audit.

Security: All operation records are encrypted at rest and signed in the audit events. Deprovision operations that touch PII include an additional retention tag and access restriction. The design preserves least privilege: provision-orch authenticates to downstream connectors with scoped service principals.

Trade-offs: Introducing provision-orch adds a new service and slightly increases SCIM write latency; we mitigate via async append and small median latency target. Finalizers add complexity to delete semantics but provide deterministic guarantees for downstream cleanup and auditing.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature flag behind 'scim_provision_orchestration' controlled per-org. 2) Enable in non-production for full e2e tests. 3) Enable for low-traffic pilot orgs and monitor metrics (operation success rate, orphan rate, audit delivery latency). 4) Gradually expand to all orgs over 2 weeks with kill-switch in place. 5) Run migration backfill for historical delete tokens after stable rollout. 6) Decommission old retry cron once operation_log proves coverage.

Rollback: Flip feature flag off; provision-orch will continue to process records already created but new SCIM writes will bypass orchestration. If we detect regression in audit delivery, pause rollouts and revert migration jobs.
test_plan: Unit tests for operation state machine and idempotency constraint
Integration tests that simulate multiple concurrent SCIM deletes for the same externalId and assert single operation created and only one downstream delete executed
Chaos test: introduce downstream ack delay and network partitions to validate quarantine path and force-delete-after TTL behavior
Load test: measure provision_log append latency at 2x expected peak and validate p95 < 150ms
E2E acceptance test that asserts audit events are written for every state transition and that audit store can be reconciled with operation_log
